newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 92 -2 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 125 +6 on last week
AMLC COMMENTARY: Cattle prices in New South Wales (NSW) and Queensland rose in the past week after useful rains and a partial recovery in the Japanese beef market.

In NSW, falls of between 25mm and 100mm occurred across many areas of the centre and north. With 37 percent of the state now drought-declared compared with 48 percent in August, expectations are that drought-declared areas may further contract in October.
Large tracts of southern Queensland also benefited from some rain over the week, although falls were less than in NSW.

Queensland yardings fell about 20 percent as a result of the rain and prices rose. Export cattle were 5-10c/kg dearer while trade cattle were firm to 5c/kg dearer. Yardings in NSW were down by about 20 percent and cattle prices rose by an average 2-4c/kg.
Cattle slaughter in Queensland last week was 43,666 head, down from 61,000 head a year ago. NSW cattle slaughter was 36,778 head, down four percent on last year.
The Western Australian (WA) season, although improving, is only fair. Significant areas of WA previously devoted to livestock are now turnoved over to forestry, where returns are higher.
With some recovery in Japan shipments to that country, while still low, are starting to increase. Japanese beef wholesale prices rose as did export prices from Australia.
Future prospects in the U.S. will depend on the cow kill over the last quarter of the year. A high kill would dampen the short-term outlook but raise longer-term prospects.
In the week ended August 24 the U.S. cow slaughter was up 33 percent from the same week of lasst year. The dairy cow slaughter was up 20 percent while the beef cow slaughter was up 45 percent.

Australian beef exports in August, at 51,658 tonnes, were 15,000 tonnes below August last year. The Japan trade suffered most with shipments totalling only 18,841 tonnes, including 12,176 tonnes of chilled beef, down from 29,246 tonnes in August 1995. Beef shipments to the U.S. continued at light levels, at only 16,084 tonnes.
